newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH COURT SENTENCES GERMAN SOCCER HOOLIGANS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH COURT SENTENCES GERMAN SOCCER HOOLIGANS.

text.p: A Polish court has sentenced three German fans to suspended six-month jail terms for burning Poland's flag and other offenses during last week's soccer friendly between the two countries, the court said on Monday.
The regional court in the southern city of Zabrze, where Germany beat Poland 2-0 last Wednesday, said in a statement that the three were also fined 600 zlotys ($220) each.
Two other fans were fined 1,850 zlotys ($685) and 1,000 zlotys ($380), it added.
The ruling was made on Friday and the five fans, whose named were not disclosed, were released, the statement said.
The behaviour by some of the German fans prompted an official telegram of apology by Bonn's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel to his Polish counterpart on Thursday.
Polish television showed live cover during the game of the German fans clashing with police, displaying anti-Semitic and anti-Polish banners and wielding sections of smashed benches.
It also showed some of them making Nazi-style salutes during the German national anthem at the Zabrze stadium.
Zabrze is about 40 km from the former death camp in Auschwitz, where Nazi German invaders murdered more than one million people, mostly Jews, during World War Two. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
